artboards.title: Main — as built, with the labelling stripped back
What it is still paying for
Direction B — one answer, then the evidence
Direction C — numbers on the first screen
The sizing review that settled the layout
Option B — rail inside today's 1,240 band
Option C — location in the frozen header

annotations.text:
WHERE THIS STARTS
The layout is settled and built: 1,482 px band, six tiles in one row, the two key plots with the project location beside them, then two rows of three, then the tables. What is left is not layout.

WHAT MAIN CHANGES
Every chart is still telling you things its own title already told you — a category axis titled "Alternative" over labels that read Alternative 1, a value axis titled "Present worth ($)" under a chart called Present worth by category, twenty-five rotated tick labels where seven would do. Main strips all of it. Nothing moves; every plot gets bigger.

THE OPEN QUESTION
Main is the safe change and I would take it either way. The question the other two artboards ask is what belongs on the first screen a reader gets.

Right now that screen is: header, project line, six tiles, verdict, two key plots, three supporting plots. No figures until you scroll. B and C each answer that differently, and the table on this artboard adds up what clears 624 px in all three.

DIRECTION B
The six tiles and the verdict banner say the same thing twice: the banner names the winner and its margin, and two of the tiles repeat both. Here it is said once, in one panel beside the plots, with the locator map at its foot.

That returns 133 px at the top of the sheet and makes the answer a paragraph rather than a wall of six numbers. The cost is that the answer no longer stays frozen while you scroll.

DIRECTION C
The results table clears the fold, so the sheet opens on figures as well as pictures. Tiles, verdict and the two key plots keep their places above it.

The cost is real: charts 3 to 8 all drop below the fold, and the sheet stops reading picture-first — which is the order it was deliberately rearranged into two rounds ago. Worth taking only if Mat's readers reach for the table first.

SETTLED LAST ROUND
The sizing review and the two alternates that were not taken. Option A — the 1,483 px band with the project location as a right-hand rail — is what got built, and Main on the Refinements page is that layout as it now stands.

Kept here because the tradeoffs are still the argument for the band being wider than a 150%-scaled window.
